summary: Canary rollout TLS handshake failures caused by private hosted-zone alias flapping to cross-account NLB during cert rotation
description: Issue summary: During an automated canary rollout of a tenant-scoped model in the customer's private deployment, a subset of inference requests fail TLS handshake intermittently (client-side TLS alert: unrecognized_name / certificate name mismatch). Failures cluster around the canary IP switch window and last ~10-90s. Impact: customer sees 5xx for ~10% of requests during canary pushes; streaming responses disconnect mid-stream. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC peered to Redwood infra-account via TGW), us-west-2, private hosted zone (customer-owned) with alias records pointing to cross-account NLB(s). Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger a canary rollout that moves a small percentage of traffic to a new NLB target group. 2) Observe DNS resolution for tenant.example.internal (customer hosted zone) during rollout. 3) Observe intermittent TLS handshake failures in serving nodes' logs and client-side error codes 524/525 equivalent in SDK telemetry. Observed logs / snippets: - Serving node TLS accept logs: "tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: illegal_parameter" (timestamps coincide with DNS changes) - Control plane telemetry: repeated trace ids showing SNI mismatch: expected 'tenant.example.internal', presented cert commonName 'nlb-rotating-*.elb.amazonaws.com'. - DNS query history (resolver): rapid A/alias responses alternating between two NLB targets within 30s.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: DNS alias and NLB certificate rotation overlapping with low-TTL DNS responses is producing a race where clients resolve to an NLB that has just begun certificate rotation, causing SNI/certname mismatch. Findings: - Private hosted zone contains two alias targets for tenant.example.internal pointing at NLB-A (account infra-123) and NLB-B (account infra-456). TTL for intermediate CNAME/alias appears low (~30s) due to customer-side automation. - AWS NLB automatic certificate provisioning/rotation for the tenant's certificate occurs asynchronously; during rotation the NLB will present a temporary certificate (wildcard for ELB domain) for a short window. - Resolver traces from customer's VPC show flapping between NLB-A and NLB-B while the canary rollout updates route tables/target groups. - Serving runtime retries typically handle connection errors but TLS alerts produced during handshake are not retried by default and surface as aborted streams. Evidence: correlating timestamps from DNS logs, NLB certificate rotation events (CloudTrail entries), and serving logs (trace id: 38b2c5a... 2026-03-10T11:23:12Z).
resolution: Workaround applied (temporary): 1) Increased alias TTL on the customer's hosted zone to 300s to reduce rapid flapping during rollouts. 2) Coordinated with customer infra to pause cross-account NLB certificate rotation during active canary windows. 3) Added a short exponential backoff+retry for TLS handshake failures in serving-runtime in the next hotfix to allow transparent retries when the error is transient. Long-term actions: - Recommend single-authoritative NLB target per tenant during rollouts or ensure zero-downtime certificate rotation (staged presentation of tenant cert). - Add detection in console for 'hosted-zone alias flapping' with automated suggestions (increase TTL / quiesce rotation). - Follow-up infra PR to add a pre-rollout readiness check that validates certificate CN on all resolved NLBs before traffic shift. Assigned follow-ups: infra team to change NLB rotation cadence; SDK team to publish patch notes for retry behavior.
